title: Polygraph — a tool that checks whether software is telling the truth
audience: General public first, contest judges second. Opens with the presenter naming the product and saying in one line what it does, so the viewer knows what they are watching before anything technical. The side-by-side speed race is held back and used later, as the payoff when the fix is introduced.
takeaway: He built Polygraph — a tool that checks whether software is telling the truth.

scenes.expression: warm, welcoming, direct to camera — introducing himself and his work to a stranger
scenes.speech: Hi, I'm Tom, and I built Polygraph. It's a tool that checks whether software is telling the truth about your computer's hardware. I pointed it at the A.I. assistant on my own laptop, and what it found genuinely surprised me.

scenes.expression: matter-of-fact, a little incredulous at what he found
scenes.speech: That assistant runs entirely offline. Nothing is sent to a company. It reported that it was using my laptop's A.I. chip, the part built to make this fast. Polygraph watched that chip and counted. It never ran. Not once.

scenes.expression: clear and confident, explaining the idea behind the tool
scenes.speech: Here's why nobody caught this. Almost every test measures how long something took, and the time looks perfectly normal either way. Polygraph doesn't measure time. It measures what actually ran, down to the individual chip instructions.

scenes.expression: decisive, setting up a demonstration — leading into the side-by-side
scenes.speech: Two hidden rules inside the code were quietly ruling it out. So I wrote a fix that picks the right setting by itself. No settings for you to learn. Same laptop, same question — here's the difference.

scenes.expression: candid, unflinching — reporting a result that undercuts his own earlier claim
scenes.speech: Then I pointed Polygraph at my own headline. On a small model my fix looked four times faster. On a seven-billion model, the size people actually run, it drops to one point three. I published that too.

scenes.expression: warm and confident, landing the real discovery
scenes.speech: But the biggest win wasn't tuning at all. On that same seven-billion model, a build that had silently lost its hardware features read prompts four and a half times slower. Polygraph finds that. It's free — point it at anything.

cards.title: A BUILD THAT LOST ITS FEATURES
POLYGRAPH
cards.value: free  ·  finds it in one command
